BUCKET 7 - DATA-INTEGRITY HARDENING: The profile object had no default-merge layer at all, unlike settings' own DEFAULT_SETTINGS + Object.assign() pattern already proven across 21+ releases of schema drift - a profile row saved by an older build, partially restored from a backup, or hand-edited in IndexedDB could be missing an entire array/object field (studyWeakPoints, actionPlan, promoPoints) rather than holding a falsy value, crashing any reader that assumes it always exists. Backup import's KV_VALIDATORS covered idp:goals, streak, calendar, and forms:saved but not the "settings" row itself - a malformed settings row (a string, number, or array instead of an object) would reach IndexedDB unvalidated, and since settings' own boot-time merge uses Object.assign({}, DEFAULT_SETTINGS, savedSettings), a string source would have its characters copied in as junk numeric-keyed properties rather than being safely ignored; added the same plain-object shape check the calendar key already uses. notifyReminders was readable throughout notify.js (both scheduleForReminder() and syncAll() gate on it) without ever being declared in DEFAULT_SETTINGS - functionally harmless since undefined is falsy and notifications are meant to default off, but left the one flag that arms a native OS permission prompt as the single settings key with no documented default; added it explicitly. Fullscreen study's focus-trap had no re-entrancy guard - enterTheater() lacked the theaterOn() early-return its own exitTheater() counterpart already had, and trapTheaterFocus() discarded its inert-element tracking array on a second call without releasing the first call's elements, which could leave sibling UI permanently unfocusable and AT-unreachable even after exiting theater mode; added the missing guard to enterTheater() and made trapTheaterFocus() always release before re-trapping.
